pages.text: $(thing)Iridescent Aptitudes$() is the pack's RPG-style leveling system, forked from the open-source $(italic)JustLeveling Fork$() mod. Eight $(bold)aptitudes$() (STR, CON, DEX, DEF, MAG, INT, BLD, LCK) gain XP from gameplay actions matching their theme, and unlock skills + passives at threshold levels.$(br2)Open the aptitude UI with the $(bold)Y$() key (or via the inventory tab if installed).

pages.title: Eight Aptitudes
pages.text: $(bold)STR$() Strength — melee damage, physical might$(br)$(bold)CON$() Constitution — HP, hunger, environment$(br)$(bold)DEX$() Dexterity — speed, agility, ranged$(br)$(bold)DEF$() Defense — armor, mitigation, knockback$(br)$(bold)MAG$() Magic — spell power, mana, magic offense$(br)$(bold)INT$() Intelligence — XP gain, knowledge, refunds$(br)$(bold)BLD$() Building — mining, reach, crafting refunds$(br)$(bold)LCK$() Luck — drop rates, jackpot procs

pages.title: Five-tier skills
pages.text: Each aptitude has $(bold)5$() skill nodes at levels $(bold)5 / 10 / 15 / 20 / 30$(). Each tier opens a new ability:$(br2)$(bold)5$() — small confidence-builder bonus$(br)$(bold)10$() — clear functional buff$(br)$(bold)15$() — bridge tier, build-defining$(br)$(bold)20$() — high-signature ability$(br)$(bold)30$() — capstone, often triggered$(br2)See the design plan in the internal repo for the full 40-slot map (8 aptitudes × 5 tiers).

pages.title: Iridescent fork — passives
pages.text: Native per-level passives (always-on, scale with aptitude level) match the redesigned themes:$(br2)$(bold)MAG$() — Spell Power (+16% spell damage at lvl 32) + Mana Regen (+32%)$(br)$(bold)INT$() — Attack Speed + Critical Chance (+25% at lvl 32; applies to melee, ranged, AND magic via the modular spellbook crit hook)$(br)$(bold)LCK$() — Luck + Critical Damage (existing — chance + damage live on different aptitudes for natural pairing)$(br2)Removed: Magic Resist + Beneficial Effect (not in design); Entity Reach on INT (replaced with crit_chance).

pages.title: Effects via KubeJS
pages.text: Tier-5/15/20/30 skill effects ship as $(thing)kubejs/server_scripts/skills/justleveling_skills.js$() handlers, not native JLFork code. Keeps gameplay logic editable without rebuilds and makes cross-mod attribute manipulation easier.

pages.title: NBT compatibility
pages.text: The fork keeps the internal modid $(italic)justlevelingfork$() so existing worlds' aptitude levels at $(thing)ForgeData.justlevelingfork.aptitude.*$() keep working through the swap — no migration needed when this jar replaces the upstream.$(br2)Stripped from the fork: gun-mod integrations (TacZ, Crayfish, Scorched Guns), the KubeJS plugin subpackage (we read NBT directly), L2Tabs inventory tab integration, BetterCombat targeting hooks, and the upstream update-check that pinged GitHub on every load.
